key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 non-routed AI matched the human's equilibria and fix but lost on depth — it never derived the firm's break-even discount (d = 20%), never located the conflict explicitly in the d >= 20% value-destroying region, and folded pay-neutrality into a single line. The v6 routed run closed all three gaps as m083 completion-contract outputs (break-even derivation, conflict-region statement, formal pay-neutrality verification) and added the m019 adversary pass's conflict-relocation finding (the profit share moves the seam to the cost line if costs become discretionary) plus the observed-quarter data-pin (the +45%/−$0.4M quarter implies d ≈ 22%, already inside the destroying region); residual shared gap: the human's pure payoff-math trace remains marginally more efficient than the gate machinery.
learning_signal: For contract-redesign tasks, equilibrium arithmetic is not the endpoint: after computing the agent's status-quo choice, the m083 contract must output (1) the principal's break-even threshold derived from both payoff functions and the location of the conflict region (the value-destroying interval), (2) verification of the redesign by recomputing the agent's OWN optimum under the new contract (a formal check, not an assertion that 'incentives align'), and (3) a pay-neutrality check at the aligned point. The m019 adversary pass must then relocate the conflict to the next seam: every contract has one (here the cost line), and a sign-matched-derivative audit is the same check at the new seam.
suggested_improvement: Keep m011+m023 dual-route with the m083 native contract on decide/estimate/maximize + adversarial signatures (router confident=no); make break-even derivation, conflict-region location, and pay-neutrality standing m083 contract items; add 'next-seam' (conflict relocation under the proposed contract) as a mandatory m019/m083 packet line so the adversary pass attacks the NEW contract's incentives, not just the old one's.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure principal-agent human baseline priced protection against a divergence it never verified — it applied the generic 2%/yr defection rate to a relationship whose 30% profit share co-aligns the agent's payoff derivative with the owner's residual, whose 9-year incident-free record and 90% retention contradict the prior, and whose pending equity grant closes the largest vector (portable client migration); its cost-benefit ($30k > $12k) excluded compliance time, the distrust signal, false-positive charges, and the outside-option loop that raises the defection probability the package prices. The v6 routed run held the protective verdict: router kept the trap style out of top-3, dual-routed m019+m039 with m003/m007/m019 gates, and ran the m083 alignment audit BEFORE costing any control — the divergence audit the pure-style baseline skipped, now installed as the P3 branch-completeness gate (source case m083).
learning_signal: Principal-agent reasoning must be bidirectional: predict misbehavior where incentives diverge, verify alignment where they appear to converge. Before any monitoring decision: (1) run the payoff-derivative alignment audit (agent's marginal take of the principal's residual) as the FIRST step — never assume divergence a priori; (2) test base-rate transferability by separating inside/outside view (m097 reference class): a generic survey rate is not evidence about a relationship whose contract and record contradict it; (3) price the monitoring instrument's full cost line — direct, compliance time, signal cost (surveillance converts an intrinsically motivated agent into a compliance-minimizing one), false positives, and the outside-option loop; (4) recommend monitoring only if prevented harm exceeds the FULL line, otherwise deepen alignment (vesting, floors, succession).
suggested_improvement: Keep m019+m039 dual-route with the m003/m007/m019 gate set on high_stakes + adversarial judgment signatures (the negative split is held); codify the divergence-audit-before-costing ordering as a standing m083 gate on ALL principal-agent and monitoring tasks, with the full monitoring-cost line (including the outside-option loop) as a mandatory packet line; retain the m097 reference-class transferability check inside the P1 provenance audit.
